activities.anchor: The Renaissance began where money and antiquity met
activities.caption: pair each conduit with what it carried into Florence
activities.name: renbConduitMatch

config.prompt: A Mediterranean contact zone, not a purely Italian reboot — pair the conduit with its cargo:

pairs.right: civic piety and dynastic display, financed
Greek scholars and manuscripts re-flooding Italy

pairs.left: Venetian trade with Islamic Central Asia
pairs.right: ultramarine, arriving to paint the sky

config.why: The tidy re-birth story hides its own trade routes: the Renaissance absorbed Arabic optics, Asian pigment and Islamic glazes while reviving its own pagan past.

activities.anchor: The style rests on a technical tripod
activities.caption: file the facts by tripod leg
activities.name: renbTripodBuckets

config.prompt: Three revolutions carried the style — file each fact:

items.label: Brunelleschi's mirror demonstration; Alberti codifies it (1435)
Masaccio's Trinity (c. 1427) — the first public painting in the new space
Van Eyck's Ghent Altarpiece (1432) — refined, not invented
slow-drying, translucent, endlessly revisable — glazes and depth
dissection legalised for artists at Florentine hospitals

config.why: Space became measurable, colour became revisable, the body gained both mechanism and ideal — plus fresco's giornata as the unit of ambition for the Sistine ceiling.

activities.caption: true or false — the oil-paint legend
activities.name: renbOilJudge

statements.s: Drying-oil media existed for centuries before Van Eyck.
statements.why: What he and the Flemish workshops did was refine the medium to a brilliance tempera could not reach.
'Perfected in Flanders' is the honest sentence — an improvement to adopt, not a secret to steal, which is why it spread so fast.

statements.s: Italy imported oil paint through Venice, which built a colour-first school on it.
statements.why: Titian's Venice is the colorito pole of the disegno-versus-colorito argument.

statements.s: Oil's slow drying made it worse for detail than tempera.
statements.why: The opposite — slow-drying and translucent layers enabled the microscope patience of the Arnolfini Portrait.

activities.anchor: Rome under Julius II assembled the impossible generation
activities.caption: drag the divider — disegno versus colorito
activities.name: renbSchoolsCompare

config.prompt: The two schools defined a 400-year argument — drag between them:

before.label: Florence & Rome: disegno
before.text: Drawing/design first — the measured world: contour, construction, ideal proportion; Michelangelo's terribilità, Raphael's equilibrium.

after.label: Venice: colorito
after.text: Colour/flesh first — oil glazes and saturation tempera never had; Van Eyck's northern realism meets Titian's colour-first school.

config.why: Flemish realism grounded in oil glazes and dense symbolism versus Italian measure — the argument European art would replay for four centuries.

activities.anchor: Michelangelo painted the Sistine ceiling lying flat on his back
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the Sistine working conditions
activities.name: renbSistineSpot

config.prompt: This account of the ceiling contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: The Sistine ceiling took Michelangelo four years on scaffolding (1508–12).
Fresco means pigment into wet plaster — the day's section, the giornata, the unit of ambition.
He painted lying flat on his back, as every film shows.
He stood on scaffolding of his own design, head tipped back, brush raised toward the plaster.
He complained in a sonnet that the paint dripped into his face and his beard pointed at heaven.
config.correction: He stood on scaffolding of his own design — the reclining image is a later embellishment, and a physiologically impossible one for brushwork that fine.
config.why: He was writing theology in anatomy, four years on scaffolding — the pose myth hides the discipline it took.

activities.anchor: The style that follows is audience-engineering
activities.caption: fund the altarpiece — three Baroque workshops bid
activities.name: renbTrentBranch

config.root: Rome, after the Council of Trent. The brief: art must teach the illiterate, testify to the mysteries, and move the viewer. Three workshops bid for your altarpiece.

choices.label: Caravaggio — tenebrism, street-level saints, freeze-frame crisis
Bernini — gilded marble, hidden daylight, coiled motion
Rubens — abundance and motion at workshop scale

caravaggio.text: The Madonna dei Pellegrini's kneeling pilgrims scandalised for exactly the reasons it worked — saints with dirty feet at street level; doctrine rendered as an event the body responds to.

bernini.text: The Ecstasy of Saint Teresa (1647–52) stages mystic vision in gilded marble and hidden daylight; his David coils mid-action and requires the viewer to circle.

rubens.text: Counter-Reformation altarpieces by treaty — a workshop economy producing abundance and motion at scale across Flanders' borders.

config.why: Baroque drama is doctrine with a lighting rig: every diagonal, spotlight and coiled marble serves the Trent brief.

activities.name: renbDutchCloze

activities.anchor: The period's northern half turned on a theological rupture
activities.caption: rebuild the image crisis, step by step
activities.name: renbReformationOrder

config.prompt: One medium, two theologies — put the rupture in order:
items: Luther's circles keep decorations but distrust veneration
Calvinist territories remove images from churches outright
waves of iconoclasm strip entire interiors (the Netherlands, 1566)
the altarpiece economy that funded Van Eyck's successors ends
Catholic territories answer with the Baroque's reaffirmation
config.why: Purpose and audience changed by confession: the North redirected to the open market of the burgher home — the Dutch Golden Age is partly an iconoclasm effect — while the South doubled down on Church spectacle.
